clue.text: Girl's brief time in Air Traffic Control

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name; with the possessive it gives JOYS
a tick is a moment, as in 'back in a tick'

explanation.surface: A young woman's short stint working in an airport control tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here; the definition is a playful description of a pilot's hand lever that directs the aircraft through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers an aircraft with this hand lever, so it is literally the control of air traffic.

clue.text: Woolly animal

definitions.meaning: a woolly is a knitted pullover or sweater
a dairy cow of the Channel Island breed

explanation.definitionFit: A woolly is a knitted pullover, and the Channel Island breed is a dairy cow.

clue.text: Schoolgirl's anticipatory exclamation

definitions.meaning: one of the three little maids from school in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, with 's standing for is
what you say when expecting something tasty

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado's young heroine bears this name, and it is also the cry of delight before eating.

clue.text: Lorelei, perhaps — one working for a time on her hair

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
a tress is a lock of a woman's long hair

explanation.surface: The Rhine siren as a part-timer busy with her long hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is the Rhine maiden of German legend who lured boatmen to their doom while combing her golden hair; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a legendary siren, a seductive woman who lured sailors to disaster.

clue.text: Jug contains a flaw — it may need something on it

definitions.text: it may need something on it

indicators.note: contains means the jug holds the flaw inside it

parts.note: a creamer is a small jug for cream
a crack is a flaw

explanation.surface: A cracked milk jug may need a patch on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream cracker is a plain British savoury biscuit, usually eaten with butter or cheese on top, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain savoury biscuit, normally eaten with butter or cheese spread on top.

clue.text: Waffle — lawyers sent back part

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the word for lawyers from right to left

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A complaint that legal people returned a vague, padded section of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to rabbit (on) is to chatter or talk at length, the sense of 'waffle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang verbs for talking on and on about nothing much.

clue.text: Charged almost everything I have

indicators.note: almost means the word for everything loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everything
've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone billed nearly all one owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like billed but means electrically live, as a live wire is.
explanation.definitionFit: A live wire carries current, so it is electrically charged.

clue.text: Castle put up party, right?

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so the party's letters are reversed

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
moral means right in the ethical sense

explanation.surface: A question whether hosting a party at a castle was proper.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the British royal family's Scottish castle residence.

clue.text: Broadcasts are true about second prize

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
broadcasts means scattered widely, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Radio reports confirm the runner-up award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasts' looks like a noun for programmes but is the verb, scattering ARE TRUE into TREAURE, which goes about S.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it dearly, the same as to cherish it.

clue.text: Note given to fellow as tip

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a fellow of a society or college is a member of it

explanation.surface: A banknote handed to a colleague as a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to remember the waiter is an old idiom for giving a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember someone, in the idiom of service staff, is to give them a gratuity.

clue.text: Scottish attendant beginning to get sick — that's the end!

indicators.note: beginning to means take only the opening letter of the word get

parts.note: ill means sick
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A Highland servant starts to feel unwell and declares it is all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end!' is surface colour only, completing the exclamation. A gillie is the attendant who helps with hunting or fishing on a Scottish estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Highland servant, especially one guiding a sportsman stalking deer or fishing.

clue.text: Fancy first name, Ron, for a pioneer

indicators.note: fancy signals an imaginative, rearranged version of the letters

explanation.surface: A man called Ron is chosen as the trailblazer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective or verb but is the anagram signal; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler on the edge of the known land, an early explorer of new territory.

clue.text: Boast about the ultimate in perfect luxury

indicators.note: about means moving around, so the letters of the word for luxury are rearranged

parts.note: luxe means luxury, as in deluxe

indicators.note: the ultimate in means only the final letter of perfect is used

explanation.surface: Someone bragging about the finishing touch on a life of comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but rearranges LUXE into EXUL, to which the final T of 'perfect' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast and to rejoice triumphantly are close senses of gloating over success.

clue.text: On the way back racehorse, starting off unusually swiftly, fell

indicators.note: on the way back tells us to read the horse's name in the opposite direction

parts.note: Red Rum was the famous racehorse that won the Grand National three times

indicators.note: starting means taking the opening letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A racehorse heading home, setting off unusually fast, takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the verb for falling but is the old adjective meaning cruel or deadly, as in 'one fell swoop'. Red Rum, reversed, gives MURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell as an adjective means fierce and deadly, the sense of a killing intent.

clue.text: To demonstrate despair, a number invested in bolts and locks

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the number goes inside the word for bolts

parts.note: to bolt and to tear are both to rush off at speed
one is a number
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A hardware tale of a number fitted among bolts and locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolts and locks' paint door hardware, but bolts is a verb meaning dashes and locks is hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling at your own head of locks is the classic gesture of frustration and despair.

clue.text: Eat humble pie and peaches on the street

parts.note: to peach is old slang for to inform on someone, as to sing is
the Mall is a famous London street; a mall is a walk or promenade

explanation.surface: Someone eating fruit pies on a city street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peaches' looks like the fruit but is the verb to inform; 'and' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to back down and adopt a meek, apologetic tone.

clue.text: Scholarly, has rooms outside the University

indicators.note: outside means the rooms go around the letter for the university

parts.note: studios are rooms, such as small flats or workrooms
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A bookish type keeps rooms off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone devoted to learning and reading.

clue.text: Unpleasant woman loudly yearns for jewels

parts.note: cat is slang for a spiteful woman

indicators.note: loudly signals that the words are to be heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: sighs, as in sighing for a lost love, means yearns

explanation.surface: A nasty woman longs out loud for precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat's-eyes are gems showing a band of light like a cat's pupil; the homophone works only when the whole phrase is spoken together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemstones such as chrysoberyl that show a bright band of light, used in jewellery.

clue.text: Strange contrasts in a society's reports

indicators.note: strange signals that the following letters appear in an unusual, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Odd discrepancies turn up in a club's published records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like a link but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned bodies publish their proceedings as volumes so titled, like the Philosophical ones of the Royal Society.

clue.text: Way to step out in line

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a rung is a step of a ladder

explanation.surface: A dancer's road to stepping out in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'out in line' gives the sense of things strung out along a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Things strung out are spread along a row, like beads threaded on a cord.

clue.text: 16 under canvas

definitions.meaning: the answer to 16 down, meaning scholarly and absorbed
camping, read as two words, in a tent

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent means absorbed or studious, and split in two it says camping in a tent.

clue.text: Girl engineer carrying a pass

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the engineer contains the letter

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A young woman engineer holding an entry permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a permit noun but is the verb, to vanish from view.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass, as clouds or an era pass, is to fade from sight and be gone.

clue.text: A bit quiet, still audible

indicators.note: audible means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: peace is quiet and stillness

explanation.surface: A remark that something is somewhat quiet yet can still be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'even so' but is part of the noun phrase quiet, stillness.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or fragment of something, a morsel.

clue.text: It can provide fabric

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A container that supplies material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'; the abbreviation SA is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth glossy woven cloth, used for dresses and ribbons.

clue.text: O yes! Grass primarily fed to cattle

indicators.note: fed to means put inside, as food goes into the animals

parts.note: oxen are cattle

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A cheerful farmer agrees that grass is mainly what the herd eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' looks like an exclamation with 'yes!', but it is the chemical symbol, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: O is the chemical symbol for the gas we breathe.

clue.text: Green army rebuffed without being shut up

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the walling-in word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to immure is to shut someone up within walls

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests pushed back, so the army's letters are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Inexperienced troops were turned back without being imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone inexperienced or not fully grown.

clue.text: One in order, rest is in order

indicators.note: in order here means once the letters are arranged properly, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A tidy instruction that the remaining items are in their correct sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in order' plays two parts: a religious order in the definition and an arrangement signal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order, called by that title.

clue.text: Information not entirely amusing supplied during journey

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the short word for information is dropped

parts.note: info is short for information
light entertainment is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: Not-quite-funny facts handed out on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied' is a link. 'not entirely' trims INFO to INF.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of meals or films on an aircraft while it is airborne on its route.
